questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had learned Chinese for a couple of years and wanted to explore China.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, you just went to the building that they had sent in the mail and got the essential information, both told and on paper.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of volunteers were there to help. They also held an information meeting a week or two later as an intro to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Two people per room, newly renovated, really happy with it.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A lot of canteens with cheap food (10-20 RMB per meal), that was really good food!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The best option by far.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everyone got through, but it was just overly bureaucratic and too many papers with overlapping information.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You arrive on the first day and do some registration to get your student card (which you need for the dorm and the canteens etc.), and get to your dorm. You also fill out some papers and see some security videos. Then the day after or two days after you do a longer registration/the 'real' registration (?).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot of volunteers

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I wanted, but I also took Chinese courses. I know a lot of internationals taking English courses didn't get them because there is high competition for them, though mostly the Chinese history or Chinese language courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Come early, in the morning. And have every paper filled out beforehand, have photos (many of them to be sure), and a registration for the health examination ready before you arrive the first time on campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some classes were really good, some were not that good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses (AI and Life science, Developmental Biology) were very rigorous/learned a lot, others were not and I was quite disappointed in not getting anything out of the courses. Further, you need to take so many courses (around 7) that, personally, I found it hard to keep up/learn as much as I wanted in each course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lecture-based, though I only took theoretical courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry in Biology(00450282-90)
Microbiology(in English)(30450263-0)
Immunology(40450032-0)
Developmental Biology(40450123-0)
AI and Life Sciences(40450711-0)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: AI and Life Sciences I got a lot out of, even though it's only 2 ECTS. Developmental Biology was good as well. The lectures of Immunology were really low level, which I was much disappointed with, but there is no exam and you only need to explore an area within immunology yourself (I chose microglia) which was super rewarding. Microbiology had really low level (repeated a lot of basic courses like molecular biology, biochemistry) though it had some interesting points.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The Visas and Health Examinations were more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is really cheap, housing is really cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only used the sport's facilities, but there were lots of clubs that you can participate in!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything club, many, many different sports facilities, world-class!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Pick up a sport

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around (esp. Tianjin nearby), and in the holiday go to another place in China and experience the culture. Also good museums/ballet in the centre

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy, but I also know the language

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly that bachelor's students are not treated as much as adults as at UCPH, we need e.g. to ask for leave if we do not attend a lecture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, language, music

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Travel a bit, be prepared for a high academic load or choose fewer courses

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Traveling, meeting people, the language, the food, and a lot of my learning was super rewarding (e.g. AI).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The lack of freedom to not attend lectures if you do not feel you get anything out of them

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
